rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضائق indicates a temporary constraint, unlike ضيق, because the Prophet was exceptionally open-hearted; settled traits use forms such as سيد and جواد.
rows.anchor: ليدل على أن ضيق عارض غير ثابت، لأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أفسح الناس صدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in به most naturally refers to بعض; other views refer it to ما, conveying, or denial.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير في به على بعض. وقيل: على ما، وقيل: على التبليغ، وقيل: على التكذيب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: لعل may be interrogative, equivalent to هل: would the Prophet leave what exposes their foolishness and insults their gods? Three parses of كراهته are reported: that they say it, lest they say it, or because they say it.
rows.anchor: قيل ولعل هنا للاستفهام بمعنى هل، والمعنى: هل أنت تارك ما فيه تسفيه أحلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanz means abundant wealth. Their request that treasure descend, rather than be given, seeks an impossible extraordinary sign, since treasures are normally underground.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: أنزل، ولم يقولوا أعطي، لأن مرادهم التعجيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets bring signs inviting reflection, not signs compelling belief; a coercive sign came to Thamud only after rejection of the evidentiary sign and as punishment.
rows.anchor: لم يبعث الأنبياء بآيات اضطرار، إنما بعثهم بآيات النظر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Messenger a warner limits his commission to warning, not securing guidance, which belongs to God.
rows.anchor: الذي فوض إليك هو النذارة لا تحصيل هدايتهم، فإن ذلك إنما هو لله تعالى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil explains the divine description as stewardship of people’s interests and power over them; Ibn ʿAtiyya says God reckons whom He wills to believe or disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كافل بالمصالح قادر عليها. وقال ابن عطية: المحصي لإيمان من شاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse is said either to be abrogated or to remain operative; no preference is supplied.
rows.anchor: قيل: وهذه الآية منسوخة، وقيل: محكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم is a disconnected question, estimated as بل followed by a hamza: do they say he invented it?
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن أم منقطعة تتقدر ببل، والهمزة أي: أيقولون افتراه

rows.speaker: ابن القشيري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qushayri reads أم as a connected question asking whether they accept the revelation or claim it is not from God and demand a like composition.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القشيري: أم استفهام توسط الكلام على معنى: أيكتفون بما أوحيت إليك من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge follows their accusation of fabrication: it first asks for ten invented surahs, easing the demand by granting their premise.
rows.anchor: فلما نسبوه إلى الافتراء طلب منهم أن يأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات إرخاء لعنانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten surahs are requested before the single-surah challenge because Hud and Yunus are Meccan while al-Baqara is Medinan; a challenger first asks for many comparable acts, then reduces the demand to one.
rows.anchor: وإنما عين بقوله: مثله، في حسن النظم والبيان وإن كان مفترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثل modifies singular, dual, or plural; used in the singular with multiple things it implies like each of them, so each requested surah should resemble a Qur’anic surah.
rows.anchor: ومثل يوصف به المفرد والمثنى والمجموع كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says ten fabricated surahs give maximal latitude: only composition remains to imitate, unlike a challenge to match the Qur’an’s unseen matters, arrangement, promises, and warnings.
rows.anchor: وقع التحدي في هذه الآية بعشر لأنه قيدها بالافتراء، فوسع عليهم في القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects construing the challenge as ten surahs answered by ten, which would fit a one-for-one challenge instead.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى عارضوا عشر سور بعشر، لأن هذه إنما كانت تجيء معارضة سورة بسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara challenges doubters with complete likeness, while Hud answers the accusation of fabrication by challenging composition; the challenges differ in purpose.
rows.anchor: ولا يزيل الريب إلا العلم بأنهم لا يقدرون على المماثلة التامة. وفي هذه الآية إنما التكليف بسبب قولهم: افتراه

rows.speaker: قائل هذا القول
rows.claim: Some say this challenge preceded the others and the whole surah must be fabricated; the author rejects this for overlooking the difference between complete likeness and arrangement.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: هذه مقدمة في النزول على تلك، ولا يصح أن تكون السورة الواحدة إلا مفتراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here مثله denotes likeness to a portion of the Qur’an, not a demand for ten-surah responses.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: مثله، لا يراد به المثلية في كون المعارض عشر سور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas names ten requested surahs from al-Baqara through Hud; the author doubts it because most are Medinan and could not be referenced in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أن السور التي وقع بها طلب المعارضة لها هي معينة البقرة، وآل عمران، والنساء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes “if they do not answer you” as addressing the Messenger honorifically, corresponding to a singular variant elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون خطابا للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على سبيل التعظيم، كما جاء فإن لم يستجيبوا لك قاله: مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the invitees as the ones who must respond: if those summoned cannot answer the challenge, accept the proof.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك أي فإن لم يستجب من تدعونه إلى المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to answer shows the Qur’an came from God with miraculous composition and reports of unseen matters, establishes His exclusive divinity, and should prompt submission.
rows.anchor: واعلموا أنه من عند الله وأنه أنزل ملتبسا بما لا يعلمه إلا الله من نظم معجز للخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “for you” may include the Messenger and the believers.
rows.anchor: ولكم الضمير جمع يشمل الرسول والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning contradictions about revelation, the passage turns to the worldly course and final outcome of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها، أنه تعالى لما ذكر شيئا من أحوال الكفار المناقضين في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is general for anyone seeking worldly adornment, but reward remains subject to God’s will, as in the verse about the immediate life.
rows.anchor: وظاهر من العموم في كل من يريد زينة الحياة الدنيا، والجزاء مقرون بمشيئته تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid applies the warning to unbelievers and believers who perform deeds for show.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي في الكفرة، وفي أهل الرياء من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: معونة
rows.claim: The source says Maʿuna, after hearing the Prophet’s statement about show-offs, recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب معونة حين حدث بقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المرائين

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas applies the verse to Jews and Christians; Ibn ʿAtiyya says they are included without being its only referents. Another view applies it to hypocrites who fought alongside the Messenger and received a share of spoils.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس: هي في اليهود والنصارى. قال ابن عطية: ومعنى هذا أنهم يدخلون في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intent is apparently righteous deeds done solely for worldly gain without belief in the afterlife; God repays unbelievers’ good deeds in this life.
rows.anchor: يقصد بأعماله التي يظهر أنها صالحة الدنيا فقط، ولا يعتقد آخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates ostentation through conspicuous, lengthened prayer, public charity for praise, and displaying knowledge for worldly standing; concealed charity is the contrast, as in a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: إذا صلى إماما يتنغم بألفاظ القرآن، ويرتله أحسن ترتيل، ويطيل ركوعه وسجوده

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads إنما نزل with doubled nūn and zāy; ما may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun with an omitted object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: إنما نزل بفتح النون والزاي وتشديدها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers have نوف; Talha ibn Maymun reads يوف in third person, Zayd ibn ʿAli reads a light يوف, and passive تُوَفْ with nominative أعمالهم is also reported.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: نوف بنون العظمة، وطلحة بن ميمون: يوف بالياء على الغيبة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ calls كان extra to explain the jussive response; the author objects that يريد would then need jussive marking and that a past condition can take a present response without كان.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن الفراء أن كان زائدة، ولهذا جزم الجواب. ولعله لا يصح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads نوفي with light fāʾ and retained yāʾ; it may be jussive with an estimated vowel in a dialect or indicative as in a poem.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: نوفي بالتخفيف وإثبات الياء، فاحتمل أن يكون مجزوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the Fire to these people most clearly indicates unbelievers; if ostentatious believers are included, it means the Fire is their due, though God may forgive them, as Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr apparently hold.
rows.anchor: والحصر في كينونة النار لهم ظاهر في أن الآية في الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ما صنعوا فيها apparently refers to the afterlife, where deeds come to nothing, but it may refer to worldly life; ما may be relative or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه عائد على الآخرة، والمجرور متعلق بحبط، والمعنى: وظهر حبوط ما صنعوا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: باطل reinforces the stated nullification; it may begin a new clause or be a second predicate, with corresponding analyses of ما كانوا.
rows.anchor: وباطل وما بعده توكيد لقوله: وحبط ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads وبطل as a past verb; Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read وباطلا in the accusative, parsed as an object of يعملون with ما extra, though the syntax is disputed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: وبطل جعله فعلا ماضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invalid deeds deserve no reward because they were not done with a sound intention.
rows.anchor: وحق أن يبطل أعمالهم لأنها لم تعمل لوجه صحيح، والعمل الباطل لا ثواب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question contrasts those seeking God’s approval with those seeking worldly life; its omitted comparison is “like them.” It conveys confirmation and a great difference in rank.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر حال من يريد الحياة الدنيا ذكر حال من يريد وجه الله تعالى بأعماله الصالحة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the groups cannot match in rank; the people with evidence include Jewish converts such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, whose proof is a divine, rational demonstration of Islam’s truth.
rows.anchor: وأراد بهم من آمن من اليهود كعبد الله بن سلام وغيره، كان على بينة من ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence is a proof from God and a demonstration that Islam is true; a witness may then testify to its validity.
rows.anchor: كان على بينة من ربه أي: على برهان من الله تعالى وبيان أن دين الإسلام حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis takes باطلا as a verbal noun based on بطل, making ما the subject: their work amounts to invalidity.
rows.anchor: معنى المصدر على بطل بطلانا ما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: These authorities identify the person on clear evidence as Muhammad and the believers, with proof being the Qur’an or Messenger; the attached pronoun is intensive.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب، وابن عباس، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والضحاك: محمد والمؤمنون جميعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والنخعي ومجاهد والضحاك وأبو صالح وعكرمة
rows.claim: These authorities identify the witness as Gabriel; al-Hasan ibn ʿAli says it is the Messenger, and Mujahid also says an angel charged to preserve the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والنخعي، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وعكرمة: هو جبريل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other identifications are ʿAli, the Gospel, Qur’an, its inimitability, the Prophet’s appearance, and Abu Bakr; a report applies the witness to ʿAli himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو علي بن أبي طالب. وروى المنهال عن عبادة بن عبد الله، قال علي كرم الله وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in منه may refer to religion, Messenger, or Qur’an; يتلوه may mean follows or recites. The Torah is named because Jews and Christians both acknowledge it as divine, unlike the Gospel.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منه يعود إلى الدين أو إلى الرسول، أو إلى القرآن. ويتلوه بمعنى يتبعه، أو يقرؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers a contrast of unbelievers and believers: the witness is Qur’an, “from Him” refers to God, and the believer combines rational proof with agreement between Qur’an and Torah; إماما is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر في تفسير هذه الآية أنه تعالى لما ذكر الكفار وأنهم ليس لهم إلا النار

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Jubayr says الأحزاب are all religious communities; Qatada says Jews and Christians, al-Suddi Quraysh, and Muqatil several Meccan clans. Al-Zamakhshari says Meccans and allied opponents; Fire is their promised destination.
rows.anchor: والأحزاب جميع الملل قاله: ابن جبير، أو اليهود، والنصارى، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn’s statement that they heard a book sent after Moses and the Negus’s comparison support shared testimony to the Torah and Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وهذا يجري مع قول الجن: إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce مرية with kasra, the Hijazi form; al-Sulami, Abu Rajaʾ, Abu al-Khattab al-Sudusi, and al-Hasan use damma, the dialect of Asad and Tamim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: في مرية بكسر الميم، وهي لغة الحجاز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the factions are Meccans; another view takes them as all unbelievers, doubting, ignorant, or defiant.
rows.anchor: الناس أهل مكة قاله: ابن عباس، أو جميع الكفار من شاك وجاهل ومعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that no one is more unjust than a fabricator answers their earlier accusation; fabricators attribute a child and partners to God and legislate without His law.
rows.anchor: لما سبق قولهم: أم يقولون افتراه، ذكر أنه لا أحد أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presentation before God exposes and disgraces them, although obedient and disobedient alike are presented; الأشهاد may be angels, prophets, believers, or witnesses borne by their limbs.
rows.anchor: وعرضهم على الله بمعنى التشهير لخزيهم والإشارة بكذبهم، وإلا فالطائع والعاصي يعرضون على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هؤلاء belittles them and على ربهم recalls that they lied against their benefactor and sovereign. Al-Zamakhshari assigns the curse and ensuing statement to witnesses; the author allows the curse as God's direct speech.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: هؤلاء إشارة إلى تحقيرهم وإصغارهم بسوء مرتكبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated وهم reinforces the clause; معجزين means they could not escape punishment, but God delayed it, and they had no protectors.
rows.anchor: وهم تأكيد لقوله: وهم، وقوله: معجزين، أي كانوا لا يعجزون الله في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is multiplied because they combine denial of resurrection, lying about God, turning people from His path, and trying to make the straight path crooked.
rows.anchor: لأنهم جمعوا إلى الكفر بالبعث الكذب على الله، وصد عباده عن سبيل الله، وبغي العوج لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع may describe worldly refusal to hear Qur’an and Messenger, illustrated by Tufayl stuffing his ears and Quraysh elders blocking listeners; alternatively it describes their inability to hear or see beneficially under multiplied punishment.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع إخبار عن حالهم في الدنيا على سبيل المبالغة يعني: السمع للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes كانوا refer to their alleged allies and idols: beings that cannot hear or see cannot truly protect anyone; ما may also be a verbal noun with an omitted preposition, which al-Farraʾ permits but the author finds strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في كانوا عائد على أولياؤهم آلهتهم أي: فما كان لهم في الحقيقة من أولياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats inability as a metaphor for extreme unwillingness to hear truth; Abū Ḥayyān objects to using ordinary speech about something unbearable as proof people lack capacity.
rows.anchor: أراد أنهم لفرط تصامهم عن اتباع الحق وكراهتهم له كأنهم لا يستطيعون السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose their souls by trading worship of God for idols; “souls” implies lost comfort or happiness, since their persons remain punished. Their fabricated gods and expected intercession fail them.
rows.anchor: كونهم اشتروا عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى، فخسروا في تجارتهم خسرانا

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh analyze لا جرم as a fixed compound meaning “indeed,” with the following clause raised as its subject.
rows.anchor: مذهب الخليل وسيبويه أنهما ركبا من لا وجرم، وبنيا، والمعنى: حق

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi treats جرم as negated by لا, nominative as a topic, with أن and its clause as predicate; other grammarians take the construction to mean inevitably or no opposition/prevention.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: جرم منفي بلا بمعنى حق، وهو مبني مع لا في موضع رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects compounding. Another analysis makes جرم a past verb meaning earned, with an implicit subject and the following clause as object; poems illustrate that root. Al-Nahhas and al-Farraʾ report dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وجرم فعل ماض معناه كسب، والفاعل مضمر أي كسب هو، أي: فعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the greatest losers because their loss lasts forever, unlike sinners whose punishment ends and gives way to relief.
rows.anchor: فإن خسرانهم لا انقطاع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing unbelievers’ fate as Fire, the passage gives believers’ fate as Paradise; the two teams are believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما يؤول إليه الكفار من النار، ذكر ما يؤول إليه المؤمنون من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison starts with the unbeliever as blind and deaf because unbelievers were mentioned first; it can also be two pairs, blind versus seeing and deaf versus hearing.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تقدم ذكر الكفار وأعقب بذكر المؤمنين، جاء التمثيل هنا مبتدأ بالكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story sequence resembles al-Aʿraf: Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot before Abraham because of Lot’s people, then Shuʿayb and Moses with Aaron; commentators offer reasons for retelling the stories.
rows.anchor: بدىء فيها بنوح، ثم بهود، ثم بصالح، ثم بلوط، مقدما عليه إبراهيم بسبب قوم لوط

rows.speaker: النحويان وابن كثير
rows.claim: Two grammarians and Ibn Kathir read أَنِّي with fatḥ, while the other seven readers use kasra, supplying an elided verb of saying. Abu ʿAli calls fatḥ a shift to direct address; Ibn ʿAtiyya says it is quoted speech, not a true shift.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النحويان وابن كثير: أني بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worship none but God” shows Noah’s people worshipped idols; أن لا may be explanatory or depend on the mission or warning. Calling the day painful is figurative because pain occurs in it, not by it.
rows.anchor: وأن لا تعبدوا إلا الله ظاهر في أنهم كانوا يعبدون الأوثان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also treats the day’s being painful as figurative; Abū Ḥayyān says attribution is literal if أليم describes painful punishment, but figurative if it names the sufferer.
rows.anchor: فإذا وصف به العذاب؟ (قلت) : مجازي مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people reject his prophethood because he is human, apparently adopting the Brahmin denial of human prophets; they belittle poor followers and deny Noah any advantage.
rows.anchor: واستبعدوا أن يبعث الله رسولا من البشر، وكأنهم ذهبوا إلى مذهب البراهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive wording about followers emphatically implies no socially distinguished person joined them; أراذل is a plural form whose derivation is discussed.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: إلا الذين هم أراذلنا، مبالغة في الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls the followers weavers and barbers; al-Nahhas calls them poor, without status or lineage, and in low-status trades. In Heraclius’s report the weak follow prophets because elites are constrained by status and pride.
rows.anchor: إنهم كانوا حاكة وحجامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نراك may mean seeing or knowing. Al-Zamakhshari says “a human like us” implies elites deserved prophethood more, or a prophet should be an angel; Abū Ḥayyān says that implication is not evident.
rows.anchor: ونراك يحتمل أن تكون بصرية، وأن تكون علمية

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وعيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr and ʿIsa read بادىء with hamza, “at first thought”; the other seven read بادي, “apparent,” which may represent a softened hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو، وعيسى الثقفي: بادىء الرأي من بدأ يبدأ ومعناه: أول الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بادئ الرأي is parsed as an adverb governed by نراك, اتبعك, or أراذلنا: outwardly, at first sight, or followers who joined without reflection, censuring unconsidered judgment. Al-Zamakhshari similarly explains it as an immediate view.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أنه منصوب على الظرف، والعامل فيه نراك أو اتبعك أو أراذلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make بادي الرأي an adjective of بشر, a circumstantial description of Noah as lacking judgment, a taunting vocative, or verbal noun. If governed by نراك or اتبعك after إلا, its syntax is problematic unless treated as an adverb.
rows.anchor: وبادىء الرأي ليس واحدا من هذه الثلاثة. وأجيب بأنه ظرف، أو كالظرف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some read بادي الرأي as a taunting vocative to Noah, saying his thoughts are obvious to everyone and thereby challenging him.
rows.anchor: يا بادي الرأي، أي ما في نفسك من الرأي ظاهر لكل أحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing makes بادي الرأي a verbal noun, although using the active-participle form for a verbal noun or adverb is not regular.
rows.anchor: وقيل: انتصب على المصدر، وجاء الظرف والمصدر على فاعل، وليس بالقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرأي may mean eyesight or thought; the خطاب لكم includes Noah and his followers, whom the speakers say do not surpass them in wealth or lineage.
rows.anchor: فالرأي هنا إما من رؤية العين، وإما من الفكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The denial of فضل is glossed as no superiority in form or character; other explanations mention wealth, kingdom, following Noah, or distinction fit for prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في الخلق والخلق، وقيل: بكثرة الملك والملك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses نظنكم as certainty; Muqatil takes it as thinking Noah’s claim and followers’ belief are false, while another view accuses them of seeking leadership and fame.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نظنكم نتيقنكم، وقال مقاتل: نحسبكم أي في دعوى نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human equality does not prevent prophethood; Noah states his certain proof hypothetically to invite acknowledgment and establish the case without a direct claim they would reject.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن المساواة في البشرية لا تمنع من حصول المفارقة في صفة النبوة والرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina means proof; interpretations of bestowed mercy include prophethood, guidance, divine enabling, and wisdom, associated with Ibn ʿAbbas, Muqatil, and others.
rows.anchor: والبينة البرهان، والشاهد بصحة دعواه ابن عباس الرحمة والنبوة مقاتل الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof and mercy are apparently distinct: proof may be a miracle and mercy prophethood, though they may be one blessing; من عنده emphasizes divine source.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن البينة غير الرحمة، فيجوز أن يراد بالبينة المعجزة، وبالرحمة النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فعميت عليكم apparently refers to the proof, blaming them for failing to recognize a clear miracle; the mercy clause is parenthetical if the two are distinct.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير عائد على البينة، وبذلك يحصل الذم لهم من أنه أتى بالمعجزة الجلية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues for dual فعميتا if proof and mercy are both antecedents; Abū Ḥayyān says the second can be omitted. العماء names a cloud because it hides what is within.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: حقه أن يقال: فعميتا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows detaching the second object pronoun, as in أنلزمكم إياها; Ibn Malik prefers connection, Ibn Abi al-Rabi requires it when the addressee comes first, and Abū Ḥayyān cites Sibawayh in support.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون الثاني منفصلا كقولك: أنلزمكم إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araytum’s omitted first object is estimated as the proof from God; Arabs use two objects and an interrogative second object in the sense “inform me.” The conditional syntax has competing verbs seeking the same object.
rows.anchor: فمفعول أرأيتكم محذوف والتقدير: أرأيتكم البينة من ربي إن كنت عليها أنلزمكموها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explicitly requires connection when the addressee is first among two objects and the absent person second, supporting Ibn Abi al-Rabi against al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Malik.
rows.anchor: فبدأت بالمخاطب قبل الغائب، فإن علامة الغائب العلامة التي لا يقع موقعها إياه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports Abu ʿAmr shortened the mīm vowel to near-sukūn and calls full sukūn incorrect except in poetry; Abū Ḥayyān says the report describes a clipped vowel.
rows.anchor: وحكى عن أبي عمرو إسكان الميم، ووجهه أن الحركة لم تكن إلا خلسة خفيفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Basran grammarians prohibit dropping inflectional vowels except in verse; Sibawayh described Abu ʿAmr as shortening the vowel, while al-Kisaʾi and al-Farraʾ report sukūn.
rows.anchor: أجمع النحويون البصريون على أنه لا يجوز إسكان حركة الإعراب إلا في ضرورة الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to al-Zamakhshari’s disparagement of expert readers, who would not confuse a clipped vowel with no vowel.
rows.anchor: والزمخشري على عادته في تجهيل القراء وهم أجل من أن يلتبس عليهم الاختلاس بالسكون

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas proposes أنوحيها عليكم as a reading, which Abū Ḥayyān calls wrong.
rows.anchor: أنوحيها عليكم، وقوله في ذلك خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah softens his appeal with “my people,” like Abraham’s “my father” and the believer from Pharaoh’s household addressing “my people.”
rows.anchor: ويا قوم استدراجا لهم في قبول كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in عليه may refer to the warning, religion, call to monotheism, or conveying the message; the explanations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليه عائد إلى الإنذار. وإفراد الله بالعبادة المفهوم من قوله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah seeks no payment because his reward is from God; he will not expel believers for their faith, as the leaders requested to avoid equality with the poor. Quraysh made a similar demand of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وكانوا سألوا منه طرد هؤلاء المؤمنين رفعا لأنفسهم من مساواة أولئك الفقراء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads tanwīn on بطارد as regular for an active participle expressing present or future action; Abū Ḥayyān says attachment may be basic because it resembles nouns and verbs.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: بطارد بالتنوين، قال الزمخشري: على الأصل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The believers meet God for judgment: He might punish Noah for wrongful expulsion or reward their sincere faith; Noah need not inspect their hearts. The author says the objectors are ignorant of consequences, believers, or the impropriety of their proposal.
rows.anchor: معناه أنهم يلاقون الله فيعاقب من طردهم، أو يلاقونه فيجازيهم على ما في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Noah asks who would defend him from God’s punishment if he expelled believers from accepted goodness or because of their faith; the rhetorical question calls them to reflect.
rows.anchor: استفهام معناه لا ناصر لي من عقاب الله إن طردتهم عن الخير الذي قد قبلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تزدري is derived with dāl replacing tāʾ; its relative object is omitted, meaning their eyes deem the believers insignificant, as poems illustrate.
rows.anchor: والعائد على الموصول محذوف أي: تزدرونهم، أي: تستحقرهم أعينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن يؤتيهم is governed by “I do not say”; لِـ means “for,” not a recipient marker, which would require “you.” Contempt cannot reduce their reward; God knows their inner selves, and Noah would be unjust to expel them.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت اللام للتبليغ لكان القياس لن يؤتيكم بكاف الخطاب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses جادلتنا as “you called us”; others say “you admonished us” or argued every way without proving the claim. Ibn ʿAbbas reads a verbal noun, with a parallel about human argumentation.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: دعوتنا، وقيل: وعظتنا، وقيل: أتيت بأنواع الجدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand the promised punishment; ما may be relative with an omitted object or a verbal noun. Noah debated throughout his mission of 950 years while they persisted in idol worship.
rows.anchor: وإنما كثرت مجادلته لهم لأنه أقام فيهم ما أخبر الله به ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment belongs to God, not Noah; if divine wisdom requires haste, they remain in God’s grasp and cannot escape or resist.
rows.anchor: إنما هو للإله الذي يعاقبكم على عصيانكم إن شاء أي: إن اقتضت حكمته أن يعجل عذابكم

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر الثقفي
rows.claim: ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar reads نصحي with fatḥ as a verbal noun; the majority’s damma may be a verbal noun or a noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر الثقفي: نصحي بفتح النون، وهو مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conditions are arranged in reverse logical order: if Noah advises them it will not help, and if God wills to misguide them, it will still not help.
rows.anchor: وصار الشرط الثاني شرطا في الأول، وصار المتقدم متأخرا، والمتأخر متقدما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the second condition’s answer is indicated by “my advice does not help”; Ibn ʿAtiyya treats it as parenthetical, rhetorically juxtaposing human and divine wills.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: قوله إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم جزاؤه ما دل عليه قوله: لا ينفعكم نصحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غوى normally means going astray, so ascribing misguidance to God argues against the Muʿtazila, who say the servant causes his own error. Al-Zamakhshari explains misguidance as leaving persistent unbelievers to their choices; Abū Ḥayyān objects to his wording about God knowing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن معنى يغويكم يضلكم من قوله: غوى الرجل يغوي وهو الضلال

rows.speaker: معتزلي
rows.claim: A Muʿtazili may read إن as negation, “God does not will to misguide you,” taking Noah’s statement as consolation that advice cannot overcome their persistence.
rows.anchor: وللمعتزلي أن يقول: لا يتعين أن تكون إن شرطية، بل هي نافية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and others report meanings of غوى related to illness, loss of milk, or near-starvation; Ibn al-Anbari rejects “destroy,” Makki denies its Arabic use, and Abū Ḥayyān rebuts them with linguistic reports.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى يغويكم يهلككم، والغوى المرض والهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If يغويكم means destroy, the wording proves neither side in theology; with the usual meaning, entrenched unbelief leaves them beyond advice and divine favors. Calling God their Lord recalls His care; returning to Him is a warning.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان معنى يغويكم يهلككم، فلا حجة فيه لا لمعتزلي ولا لسني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take the fabrication accusation as an interruption referring to Quraysh and Muhammad; Abū Ḥayyān says the report lacks a sound chain.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذه الآية اعترضت في قصة نوح، والأخبار فيها عن قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent reading makes “they” Noah’s people, accusing him of inventing what he taught about God’s religion and punishment.
rows.anchor: ولكن الظاهر أن الضمير في يقولون عائد على قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتأس is derived from البؤس and describes distress when a person hears something painful.
rows.anchor: وابتأس افتعل من البؤس، ويقال: ابتأس الرجل إذا بلغه شيء يكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Kufan syntactic analysis of the active reading, God made Noah despair of their faith, which revelation makes effectively impossible.
rows.anchor: على مذهب الكوفيين، أيأسه الله من إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s revelation made Noah despair of further conversions; إلا من قد آمن means only those from whom expected faith had already appeared. ابتأس describes resigned grief over their denial and hostility, as four poems illustrate.
rows.anchor: أيأسه الله من إيمانهم، وأنه صار كالمستحيل عقلا بإخباره تعالى عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Under Our eyes” means God observes, guards, and protects the ark’s construction; the plural intensifies continuing care, as a singular form appears elsewhere. Talha reads an assimilated variant.
rows.anchor: بأعيننا بمرأى منا، وكلاءة وحفظ فلا تزيغ صنعته عن الصواب فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ووحينا means God inspires how to build; Ibn ʿAbbas says Noah did not know shipbuilding, so God showed him to make the vessel like a bird’s breast.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: لم يعلم كيف صنعة الفلك، فأوحى الله أن يصنعها مثل جؤجؤ الطائر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “Our eyes” literally as angels assigned to guard and help Noah; interpreting “Our revelation” as merely command or knowledge is weak because the imperative already says that.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل قوله بأعيننا أي بملائكتنا الذين جعلناهم عيونا على مواضع حفظك ومعونتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls Gabriel the زان of Noah’s ship, meaning its construction supervisor. Noah is forbidden to intercede for the wrongdoers because they are sentenced to drown; another view identifies his wife and son.
rows.anchor: كان زان سفينة نوح جبريل
